statement: SDL 3.2.0's Linux evdev backend conditionally maps the four Xbox Elite paddle slots when a Microsoft-vendor device advertises all of BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY5 through BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY8. Linux v7.3 xpad instead advertises the original Elite paddles as BTN_GRIPR, BTN_GRIPR2, BTN_GRIPL, and BTN_GRIPL2, which are different key codes. Therefore that SDL 3.2.0 automatic evdev paddle-mapping condition does not match the pinned xpad Elite event surface; no runtime mapping acceptance was measured.

applicability.scope: SDL release-3.2.0 SDL_sysjoystick.c:2655-2675 requires BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY5 (0x2c4) through BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY8 (0x2c7); it has no BTN_GRIP key handling. Linux v7.3 xpad.c:470-475, 2001-2005 advertises BTN_GRIPL (0x224), BTN_GRIPR (0x225), BTN_GRIPL2 (0x226), BTN_GRIPR2 (0x227), not matching the SDL condition. This gap concerns automatic paddle slot mapping, not ordinary gamepad button/axis recognition. Explicit SDL mapping database entries or user overrides may expose the grip buttons, but none was tested here.
